issues.title: Bound native decoding and remeasure real APFS resource use
issues.body:
## Outcome

Make native decompression interruptible within a measured resource bound before the exact iOS 14/15 first-tooling gate can pass.

## Evidence

The current KernelCache/DeviceTree adapter calls `lzfse-cgo.DecodeBufferInto` synchronously. Go context cancellation is checked before and after component reads, but cannot stop that C call once entered. Its input/output buffers are bounded (KernelCache 128 MiB each; DeviceTree 16 MiB each), yet native allocation and execution time have no hard process limit. The exact verified iPhone12,1 iOS 14/15 inspections observed peak RSS of 145,457,152 and 207,708,160 bytes respectively while disk/APFS parsing stopped at upstream UDIF codec [go-apfs-v3 #146](https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-apfs-v3/issues/146). Those runs do not measure the real APFS path after the codec is fixed. [PR #53](https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-ios-vm/pull/53) records the resource budget and fixed-path limits.

## Work

- Bound interruption of synchronous native payload decoding, for example through a killable isolated worker or a proven equivalent. Preserve the current byte caps and source/evidence semantics.
- Re-run the exact two verified images after #146 advances UDIF parsing, measure process RSS/CPU and disk/staging demand, and set a defensible operational limit or explicit refusal path.
- Keep cancellation, timeout, resource exhaustion, and partial coverage distinct. Do not mark a run complete after a worker is killed or a codec fails.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A deliberately stalled or oversized native decode is interrupted within a documented bound; no worker or temporary file is left behind.
- [ ] The exact pinned iOS 14/15 pair has updated host measurements after the UDIF codec change, or a further format blocker is linked with truthful partial coverage.
- [ ] PostgreSQL/CLI integration, cancellation and failure-injection tests pass on macOS and Linux; `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass.

## Coordination

Priority P0 release blocker for [go-ios-vm #20](https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-ios-vm/issues/20). Depends on resource-budget issue #19 and upstream go-apfs-v3 #146 for the real-image measurement. Do not commit proprietary firmware bytes.

- [ ] Existing database configuration starts the app; DB failure has a safe visible diagnostic.
- [ ] Only local clients connect; no secret or write endpoint is exposed; shutdown releases listener and pool.

#### Verification
Go `httptest` and an isolated PostgreSQL schema cover startup, health, routing and shutdown; test non-loopback refusal, error redaction and `go test ./...`/`go vet ./...`. Document the command and port behavior.

issues.title: go-ios-vm: local inspection UI baseline
issues.body:
<!-- weave-backlog:go-ios-vm-inspection-ui:v1:INDEX -->
Backlog ID: `INDEX` · Source: 2026-10-22 user UI request and answers; repository `main` `e8e2011`; [README](https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-ios-vm/blob/e8e2011/README.md), [inspection architecture](https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-ios-vm/blob/e8e2011/docs/inspection-architecture.md), [evidence model](https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-ios-vm/blob/e8e2011/docs/evidence-model.md), and the ADRs linked below.

#### Purpose and scope
Add a local browser app served by the Go CLI so an analyst can observe running CLI work, search and browse PostgreSQL inspection results, and visually review source-backed IPSW relationships. This UI blocks #20. It is read-only; hosted collaboration, arbitrary SQL, VM execution, finding edits and assessment edits are outside this phase.

#### Product baseline
1. Serve on loopback by default with existing Viper database configuration; never send a DSN or credentials to the browser. Source: user decision and README.
2. Show committed acquisition/inspection progress, coverage, interruption, stale/crashed, failure, cancellation, partial and complete states. Percentages require measured totals. Source: user request, architecture and #16/#17.
3. Search exact targets, artifacts, runs, components, observations, findings/revisions/assessments, source locations and retained evidence from PostgreSQL after cache pruning. Bound pages and byte previews. Source: user request, evidence model, [ADR 0003](https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-ios-vm/blob/e8e2011/docs/adr/0003-postgresql-evidence-store.md).
4. Draw only typed relationships backed by selected-target records: manifest components, device-tree structure, declared driver dependencies, supported APFS paths, and finding/evidence basis. Distinguish interpretations and coverage; never infer cross-target equivalence from matching names. Source: user request and evidence model.
5. Validate the UI on the exact iPhone12,1 iOS 14/15 pair before #20 can close; format gaps remain explicit. Source: user decision, #20, [ADR 0002](https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-ios-vm/blob/e8e2011/docs/adr/0002-codec-capabilities-in-go-apfs.md).

#### Glossary
`Target` is one exact manifest identity; `run` is an attempt; `observation` is a source-scoped reading; `finding` is a target/subject/property question; `revision` is one answer; `assessment` reviews that revision; `coverage` describes examined scope; `source location` names a logical decoded view or range. Unknown, absent, unexamined, unsupported and zero are distinct.

#### Agreed architecture decisions
[ADR 0001](https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-ios-vm/blob/e8e2011/docs/adr/0001-fresh-implementation.md): fresh implementation, no legacy UI migration. [ADR 0002](https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-ios-vm/blob/e8e2011/docs/adr/0002-codec-capabilities-in-go-apfs.md): missing disk/filesystem codecs belong in go-apfs-v3. [ADR 0003](https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-ios-vm/blob/e8e2011/docs/adr/0003-postgresql-evidence-store.md): PostgreSQL owns durable findings and supporting bytes; the UI reads that system of record. The runner does not depend on the UI or database.

| existing `Real-image inspection gate` | Existing #20 checks plus completed UI gate | #20 (external to namespace) |

| --- | --- | --- |
| Local browser, read-only | [UI-01](https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-ios-vm/issues/39) | Go CLI hosts loopback; no mutation endpoints. |

issues.title: Decode IDREF object references in iOS 14 prelinked kernel metadata
issues.body:
## Observed format gap

The verified public iPhone12,1 iOS 14.0 (18A373) archive (`SHA-256 a30f2fa8d4dbdcd2a8cf0f1644de3879019ba6f8be8fba49806a9c82dec09759`) contains selected identity 1 (`n104ap`, Customer Erase). Its `kernelcache.release.iphone12b` decodes to a Mach-O with a 1,121,340-byte `__PRELINK_INFO/__info` section. The section contains 3,383 self-closing `<integer IDREF="…"/>` elements and corresponding `<integer ID="…" size="64">…</integer>` definitions. The current `readKernel` passes the section to `howett.net/plist.Unmarshal`, which returns:

```text
plist: error parsing XML property list: invalid empty <integer/>
```

Both macOS and Linux inspection runs retain the kernel `mach_header` finding but mark `KernelCache` partial at this error. The raw kernel ZIP member and its source coordinate remain recoverable from PostgreSQL. The complete archive and local BuildManifest were independently checked in [qualification issue #10](https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-ios-vm/issues/10).

A small, safe reproducer of the parser mismatch (no firmware bytes):

```xml
<plist version="1.0"><array><integer ID="1" size="64">42</integer><integer IDREF="1"/></array></plist>
```

`howett.net/plist.Unmarshal` returns the same `invalid empty <integer/>` error for this input. Apple's [IOKitUser unserializer](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/IOKitUser/blob/main/IOCFUnserialize.tab.c) has an explicit `IDREF` grammar and object-tag table. This suggests the section uses IOKit object serialization XML rather than an ordinary property list; implement according to the actual reference semantics rather than treating the empty tag as zero.

## Requested outcome

- Decode the bounded prelink object graph with ID/IDREF references, preserving exact integer values and shared references needed for driver metadata. Keep the existing 16 MiB section limit; reject dangling or duplicate definitions and invalid types, and bound traversal of cycles without unbounded recursion or memory growth.
- Retain source coordinates and raw supporting bytes for driver findings. Do not infer missing drivers from a parse failure.
- Add small synthetic fixtures for valid shared references and malformed references. No proprietary kernel bytes in Git.
- Re-run this verified image on macOS and Linux; recover driver findings from `finding show` and document any further format gap separately.

Related: [qualification PR #22](https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-ios-vm/pull/22).

issues.title: List and search restore IPSWs before verified CLI download
issues.body:
## Outcome

Let a CLI user find an available restore IPSW for an exact device, choose a version/build from a concise list, and download that exact choice through the existing verified `firmware fetch` path.

## Work

- Add `firmware list --product PRODUCT` (with `search` as an alias or an equivalent `--search QUERY` filter) to enumerate restore IPSW candidates for the device across the current Apple restore catalog and the historical locator. Search must match version/build without requiring the user to know the exact build first.
- Return product, version, build, source, URL, declared size/checksum where present, and an explicit unverified/catalog-locator status. Release-only metadata must not look like a downloadable restore IPSW. Give text users a concise sorted result and keep versioned JSON output for automation.
- Preserve source attribution and raw catalog responses in PostgreSQL. Handle failed sources as partial results rather than silently claiming an exhaustive list; reject malformed/non-Apple URLs and duplicate or ambiguous exact selections.
- Show the documented next command for an exact row: `firmware fetch --product PRODUCT --version VERSION --build BUILD`. Fetch must retain bounded manifest probing, full size/checksum verification, SHA-256 cache naming, and local BuildManifest verification before publishing the file.
- Cover historical-only releases, query matches/no matches, source failure, and ambiguity with safe fixtures. Do not commit IPSWs.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A user can list `iPhone12,1` releases, search for `14.0`, select build `18A373`, and start the exact verified fetch without copying a URL by hand.
- [ ] The list labels unverified candidates and source failures accurately; an empty result is distinct from a complete catalog.
- [ ] Unit/integration tests and `go vet ./...` pass; documentation includes text and JSON examples and explains PostgreSQL configuration.

Persist completed inspection progress without one transaction covering the whole parse.

## Work

- Split the workflow/store contract into idempotently keyed observation batches and a separate final coverage ledger. Store effective input identity and completed component checkpoints.
- Expose explicit resume of a run against a verified matching archive; never resume against changed bytes or label unfinished coverage complete.
- Keep incomplete evidence manifests unavailable and deduplicate identical retained bytes across retries.

## Acceptance

- [ ] An interrupted run retains completed batches and a non-complete state; resuming publishes only missing work.

Allow a user to correct or interpret an observed finding while preserving the earlier reading and its evidence.

issues.body:
## Outcome

Replace the unconditional `filesystem-content: unexamined` result with bounded file inspection for the selected OS filesystem.

## Work

- Use `go-apfs-v3` for supported filesystem reads; add only workflow and source-location integration here. If a required disk/filesystem codec is missing, open the specific `go-apfs-v3` issue first, as ADR 0002 requires.

issues.title: Stage ZIP-compressed OS disk members within explicit limits
issues.body:
## Outcome

Let disk inspection borrow an OS image from a compressed IPSW ZIP member without unbounded memory or disk growth.

## Work

- Add a bounded, disposable staging reader for compressed OS members in `internal/inspection`; account for declared and measured expanded size and available disk space before and during staging.
- Preserve the transform chain from archive member to decoded disk view. Keep retained evidence tied to the encoded source bytes that can actually be recovered; do not invent physical APFS extents.
- Clean staging on success, failure, and cancellation; keep externally supplied originals and active cache leases intact.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Stored and compressed ZIP members expose the same disk metadata where supported.
- [ ] Oversized, truncated, corrupt, and cancelled staging produce explicit partial coverage and leave no reusable incomplete image.
- [ ] Small fixture tests plus `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass.

issues.body:
## Outcome

Make exact historical restore resolution usable for the agreed iPhone12,1 image pair. Current GDMF and iTunes catalog queries did not resolve either release; their no-match result is not proof that the Apple CDN image is unavailable.

## Work

- Investigate a reproducible route from requested product/version/build to each historical restore URL. Preserve the source and original response or record used for resolution; any selected download URL and redirects must pass the Apple HTTPS host check.
- Integrate the route with `firmware discover` and `firmware fetch` without treating an OTA as a restore IPSW or silently choosing a different release. Keep discovery, URL resolution, download, and BuildManifest verification distinct.
- Add bounded fixture tests for exact selection, ambiguous/no-match results, invalid hosts, and manifest mismatch.

## Acceptance

- [ ] For each requested version, publish the exact candidate build and source route, then verify product, board, variant, and build from BuildManifest before claiming a pinned image.
- [ ] If a historical route cannot be resolved, show the sources checked and leave the corresponding image issue blocked. Do not substitute another version or build.
